purpose: Map every existing Book authority related to author-required decisions before defining a queue runtime, so the queue reuses canonical AUTHOR_DECISION, Runtime V2 handoffs, Lifecycle gates and Version/Rollback authority ingestion instead of creating a second canonical, lifecycle, integration or versioning system.

canonical_author_decision_object.role: Immutable parent evidence of an explicit author decision once validly resolved.
canonical_author_decision_object.must_not_do: Do not silently edit the already-qualified Canonical State Model merely to add queue metadata. Exact subject/digest, queue lineage and concurrency evidence belong in the new queue ledger/receipts unless a separately versioned parent state model is later proven necessary.

runtime_v2_author_handoff.trigger: QUEUE_AUTHOR_DECISION or proposal author authority requirement
runtime_v2_author_handoff.hard_boundary: Runtime V2 may queue a requirement but cannot fill author_choice, mark approval, or manufacture AUTHOR_DECISION.

lifecycle_author_gate.hard_boundary: Lifecycle consumes an already-existing exact parent AUTHOR_DECISION with APPROVED status, required decision_type and affirmative applicable author_choice; no inference is permitted.

version_rollback_authority_ingest.hard_boundary: Version/Rollback may record an already-committed author-decision parent successor and exact authority receipt; it may not create or reinterpret the author decision.

publication_boundary.hard_boundary: PUBLICATION_AUTHORIZATION remains a distinct author-required decision. Technical export/proof states never synthesize it.

examples: non-subjective internal disposition that existing parent contracts already authorize without author choice
PARENT_OPERATIONAL.queue_rule: Do not route through Author Decision Queue merely because a workflow has multiple technical outcomes; retain the owning parent authority.

EXTERNAL_OR_LEGAL.queue_rule: May be tracked as an external-authority dependency but must not be represented as an author choice unless the same person legitimately holds that separate authority.

true_net_new_queue_gap: one parent-owned durable queue ledger/index for unresolved author-required handoffs from multiple Book authorities
exact subject object/version/digest and parent-state version/digest binding for every queued item
deduplication of equivalent author handoffs without losing source lineage
immutable queue-item snapshot/version lineage for material queue-state changes
author presentation state separate from canonical AUTHOR_DECISION status
explicit option identity and custom-author-option support without provider-preferred default authority
evidence/disagreement/consequence refs needed to understand the decision without copying unnecessary private content
stale/superseded decision invalidation when subject, proposal, manuscript, rights/privacy or governing constraints change
expected-current concurrency and idempotent resolution so two taps/devices cannot create conflicting author decisions
resolution receipt that binds exact queue item, exact choice, exact subject identities and exact pre/post parent identities
bounded parent commit that may append one canonical AUTHOR_DECISION but may not also promote manuscript, advance lifecycle, admit proposal, freeze export or publish
handoff from the resulting exact parent successor to Version/Rollback using authority_kind AUTHOR_DECISION
read-only consumer hooks so Lifecycle/Runtime/Export can observe current decision refs without gaining author authority
UI projection contract for concise mobile choices, review/confirmation and accessibility while keeping UI rendering in System Master Core/app layer
do_not_build: a second canonical author-decision object model
a second Runtime V2 proposal/admission queue
an AI auto-approval or model-preferred choice mechanism
provider or Prose ability to resolve an author decision
silent mutation or deletion of an already-recorded author choice

proposed_queue_ledger_boundary.canonical_decision_rule: RESOLVED is not itself lifecycle/canon/export action. Successful resolution may append exactly one canonical AUTHOR_DECISION in a separate atomic parent successor, after which owning consumers must independently validate and act.

staleness_rules_to_bind_in_contract: A queued item cannot be resolved against a different subject digest or parent projection without explicit revalidation/new queue snapshot.
A materially changed option set creates a new queue-item version; old presented choices remain historical and cannot be silently substituted.
A changed proposal/manuscript/canon/rights/privacy condition can make a pending item STALE or SUPERSEDED; prior presentation/interaction evidence remains historical.
A recorded canonical AUTHOR_DECISION remains immutable historical evidence even when later change makes it no longer current for a new subject identity.
concurrency_and_replay_rules_to_bind_in_: Resolution requires exact expected parent state and exact queue-ledger version/digest.
Same request/idempotency identity with same normalized resolution returns existing receipt without another parent commit.
Same decision request resolved concurrently to different choices fails closed and requires explicit current-state review.
Only one canonical author-decision append may result from one resolved queue-item version.
forensic_conclusion: The queue is a bounded author-authority capture and routing layer. Most semantics already exist elsewhere. The implementation should primarily add durable exact-bound pending-item management, human resolution and immutable receipts, then hand the resulting parent successor back to already-qualified Lifecycle/Runtime/Versioning consumers.
qualification_effect: NONE. Forensic mapping only; no queue runtime, human decision, canonical mutation, lifecycle transition or publication authority is created.
